Vendor Stability.content:
Notion Labs, Inc. was founded in 2013 by Ivan Zhao and Simon Last (https://research.contrary.com/report/notion).

The company's disclosed funding history includes:

	•	Seed / Early Rounds: Raised $2 million in angel funding in May 2015 and a $3.2 million Seed Plus round in June 2016 (https://startupintros.com/orgs/notion). 
	•	Series A: Raised $10 million in July 2019 at an $800 million valuation led by First Round Capital and angel investors (https://startupintros.com/orgs/notion). 
	•	Series B: Raised $50 million on April 2, 2020, at a $2 billion valuation led by Index Ventures (https://startupintros.com/orgs/notion). 
	•	Series C: Raised $275 million on October 8, 2021, at a $10 billion valuation led by Coatue Management and Sequoia Capital (https://startupintros.com/orgs/notion). Total funding raised across all rounds stands at approximately $340 million to $418 million (https://startupintros.com/orgs/notion). 
Notion grew from a lean team of under 50 employees during its early unicorn phase to over 500+ employees globally (https://medium.com/@sherrysun/notion-from-near-collapse-to-a-10b-all-in-one-workspace-unicorn-6113f7e1dc4c). During a major product rebuild in 2015, the co-founders laid off their initial 4-person team before relaunching Notion 2.0 (https://research.contrary.com/report/notion); however, no widespread company layoffs have occurred since achieving unicorn status ("no URL available for this"). Executive leadership has remained stable under co-founders Ivan Zhao and Simon Last, alongside early COO Akshay Kothari, with no high-profile executive departures reported ("no URL available for this"). There are no active shutdown rumors, insolvency signals, or acquisition threats ("no URL available for this"). Notion acted as an acquirer by buying privacy-focused email startup Skiff in February 2024 to launch Notion Mail (https://research.contrary.com/report/notion).
Vendor Stability.source_type: self-reported, corroborated by named funding sources

Incident History.content:
•	Data Breaches: No major public customer data breaches or systemic database exposures have been reported to date ("no URL available for this"). 
	•	Outages & Infrastructure: On February 12, 2021, Notion experienced a major global outage when its primary .so domain (notion.so) was temporarily locked by the registry due to a DNS registrar dispute, forcing the company to expedite its transition to notion.com (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=26113444). Notion maintains a public status page and targets a 99.9% uptime SLA for Enterprise plan customers (https://www.notion.com/security). 
	•	Lawsuits: No public class-action lawsuits or regulatory actions regarding data mishandling or security breaches exist against Notion Labs ("no URL available for this"). Privacy discussions on developer forums note potential third-party consent risks when using automated AI meeting summary tools, though no formal legal actions have been filed (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44942628).

Community Signal.content:
•	G2 & Review Platforms: Notion holds an average rating of 4.6/5 across 11,000+ reviews on G2 and 4.7/5 on Capterra (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews). 
	•	Common Praise: Users praise workspace consolidation (combining docs, wikis, and databases), flexible block-based architecture, and AI capabilities for summarizing meeting notes, autofilling database columns, and searching workspace knowledge (https://hackceleration.com/labs/review/notion) (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews). 
	•	Common Complaints: On Reddit (r/Notion) and G2, the primary complaint is the "blank canvas" problem and steep learning curve for non-technical users (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews). Other recurring technical complaints include performance slowdowns on databases exceeding 5,000 records, clunky mobile editing, and limited offline capabilities compared to local-first alternatives (https://hackceleration.com/labs/review/notion) (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews). 
	•	AI-Specific Sentiment: Community feedback on Reddit highlights friction around per-user pricing add-ons for full AI/Agent capabilities ($10–$20/user/month) and occasional hallucinated answers during workspace search (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews) (https://hackceleration.com/labs/review/notion). 
	•	User Churn / Competitors: Users switching away from Notion frequently move to Obsidian or Logseq for local-first Markdown storage and offline privacy, or to Asana, ClickUp, and Monday.com for dedicated project management and native time tracking (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=26113444) (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews).

Compliance Posture.content:
•	SOC 2 Status: Notion maintains a SOC 2 Type II report evaluating Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy over an extended audit window; this is a vendor claim independently audited by an accredited CPA firm (https://www.notion.com/security) (https://trust.notion.com/). 
	•	ISO Certifications: Notion holds independent certifications for ISO 27001 (Information Security Management), ISO 27701 (Privacy Information Management), ISO 27017 (Cloud Security), and ISO 27018 (Cloud Privacy Protection); these are vendor claims verified by external ISO registrars (https://www.notion.com/security) (https://trust.notion.com/). Notion also holds a BSI C5 cloud security attestation (https://www.notion.com/security). 
	•	GDPR: Compliant with GDPR requirements; offers a formal Data Processing Addendum (DPA) incorporating Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) (vendor claim: https://www.notion.com/security("https://www.notion.com/security")). 
	•	HIPAA / BAA Availability: HIPAA compliance is supported exclusively for Enterprise plan customers, provided admins configure recommended security controls and execute a formal Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with Notion (vendor claim: https://www.notion.com/security) (https://www.notion.com/help/security-and-privacy). 
	•	PCI DSS: Compliant as a PCI DSS Merchant Level 2 for processing subscription payments; however, vendor terms explicitly prohibit customers from storing payment card data (PCI) inside their Notion workspace pages (vendor claim: https://www.notion.com/help/security-and-privacy("https://www.notion.com/help/security-and-privacy")). 
	•	FedRAMP: Notion does not currently hold FedRAMP authorization or FedRAMP In-Process status for US federal agency deployments ("no URL available for this").

Data Handling Posture.content:
•	Data Collected & Stored: Customer content (text, blocks, database entries, uploaded files), AI prompt queries, generated AI outputs, session telemetry, and account metadata (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices) (https://trust.notion.com/). 
	•	Hosting Location: All customer data and AI vector embeddings are hosted on cloud infrastructure in Amazon Web Services (AWS) data centers (https://trust.notion.com/). 
	•	Data Retention Policy: Active account data is retained continuously. When a page or workspace is deleted, content can be restored for 30 days, after which it is permanently purged within 60 days (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices). For AI features: Enterprise plan workspaces operate under zero data retention by LLM providers during processing; non-Enterprise workspaces retain AI prompt data with LLM providers for up to 30 days before deletion (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices). Vector embeddings are purged within 60 days of workspace deletion (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices). 
	•	Model Training Policy: Customer data is strictly never used to train or fine-tune Notion AI models or third-party partner LLMs; contractual agreements with LLM vendors explicitly enforce this restriction (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices) (https://trust.notion.com/). 
	•	Subprocessors & Third Parties: Primary AI subprocessors include OpenAI (used for zero-retention embeddings and LLM inference) and Anthropic (Claude models), alongside cloud infrastructure providers AWS and Turbopuffer (vector storage) (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices). Subprocessor changes are published with advance email notification available via team@makenotion.com (https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices).

Integration Risk.content:
•	Integration Methods: Integrates via a public REST API, official client SDKs (e.g., JavaScript @notionhq/client), webhooks, and pre-built connectors for platforms like Slack, Jira, GitHub, Asana, Zapier, Nightfall DLP, and Datadog SIEM (https://www.notion.com/help/add-security-and-compliance-integrations). 
	•	Data Export & Exit Ease: Workspaces can be exported on demand in HTML, Markdown, or CSV formats (for databases) with attached file assets packaged in a ZIP archive (https://www.notion.com/help/export-your-content). Individual pages can also be exported to PDF (https://www.notion.com/help/export-your-content). 
	•	Export Policy Changes: Notion is phasing out full workspace-level PDF exports between now and August 31, 2026, while retaining full workspace HTML, Markdown, and CSV export capabilities (https://www.notion.com/help/back-up-your-data). 
	•	Integration Limits & Lock-in Risk: The Notion REST API enforces a rate limit of 3 requests per second per integration token, which can restrict large real-time data syncs (https://hackceleration.com/labs/review/notion). Vendor lock-in risk is moderate-to-high: while raw text exports cleanly as Markdown, complex relational database logic, rollups, custom formulas, and proprietary block layouts do not map 1:1 to other platforms upon export (https://hackceleration.com/labs/review/notion) (https://checkthat.ai/brands/notion-labs-inc/reviews).
